short: The defining novelist of the Victorian era, whose works exposed the squalor of industrial society.
full:
Charles Dickens experienced profound poverty in his youth when his father was imprisoned for debt, forcing him to work in a blacking factory at age twelve. This trauma fuelled a lifelong preoccupation with social injustice, poverty, and the plight of children, themes he relentlessly explored after finding phenomenal early success with The Pickwick Papers in 1836.

Over the next three decades, Dickens became an international celebrity, publishing massive, episodic novels like Oliver Twist, Bleak House, and Great Expectations that captivated readers across the English-speaking world. His vivid characterisation and passionate campaigning for social reform laid bare the harsh realities of 19th-century Britain and permanently shaped the public conscience.
